items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: Leonard Feather's review of your concert with Nat Pierce and Frankie Capp, last Sunday

ctx.x: That's right and if it wasn't written down exactly to be played that way the second time, I would never play it that way a second time. But once it has been put down and has been marked as being played that way, I can play it that many times exactly as I so desire. But if I had it my own way, I would play it just a little bit different, each and every time, which is the fruits of being a good jazz player.

Yes. I wanted to get into the record a funny thing from Leonard Feather's review of your concert with Nat Pierce and Frankie Capp, last Sunday (inaudible) Frank Katt (PHONETIC), in which he referred to you as "the grand Marshal of the alto saxophone, Marshal Royal, romantically showcased in Benny Carter's "A Souvenir," (inaudible) which was kind of nice. To go from being called a "valuable general" from the British book to the newspaper that called you the "grand Marshal of the alto saxophone."
Well, there are certain things that only happen to you after you have become a certain age. So
